title: Career Roadmap: SOC Analyst
summary: A SOC Analyst works in a Security Operations Center, where security alerts and telemetry from computers, servers, networks, cloud platforms, and security tools are monitored and investigated.

about.label: Career level
about.text: SOC Intern → Tier 1 SOC Analyst → Tier 2 Analyst → Senior Analyst / SOC Lead

about.label: Core industries
about.text: Cybersecurity services, IT, banking, healthcare, telecommunications, government, cloud services

about.label: Primary objective
about.text: Monitor security events, investigate suspicious activity, identify potential cyber threats, and help organizations detect, respond to, and document security incidents

sections.heading: What does a SOC Analyst do?

blocks.text: A SOC Analyst works in a Security Operations Center, where security alerts and telemetry from computers, servers, networks, cloud platforms, and security tools are monitored and investigated.

For example, if a company account suddenly logs in from an unusual location and attempts to access sensitive files, a SOC Analyst reviews authentication logs, checks related alerts, determines whether the activity is suspicious, and follows the organization's incident-response procedures.
Core responsibilities

items.text: Monitor alerts generated by SIEM, endpoint detection, network security, and cloud security tools.
Review authentication events, system logs, network connections, and endpoint telemetry.
Triage alerts to distinguish suspicious behavior from benign activity.
Investigate phishing reports, malware alerts, unusual logins, and possible unauthorized access.
Correlate evidence across systems and document investigation findings.
Escalate confirmed or high-risk incidents according to severity and response procedures.
Support containment, recovery, and post-incident review under authorized processes.
Maintain incident tickets, timelines, evidence records, and shift handover notes.
Tune detection rules and identify recurring false positives with senior team members.
Track emerging attack techniques and improve detection coverage.

blocks.label: Important distinction
blocks.text: A SOC Analyst focuses on monitoring, detection, triage, and incident investigation. A Penetration Tester proactively tests systems for exploitable weaknesses, while a Digital Forensics Analyst specializes in examining and preserving digital evidence. These functions can overlap, but their day-to-day responsibilities differ.

rows.text: Logs, networking, security fundamentals, lab exercises
Alert triage, initial investigation, ticketing, escalation
Incident investigation, threat correlation, detection tuning
Complex incidents, threat hunting, response coordination
SOC Lead / Security Operations Manager / Detection Engineer
Detection strategy, team leadership, security operations improvement

blocks.text: The timelines are indicative. Progress depends on practical investigation skills, shift experience, technical depth, and the employer's SOC structure.

This plan assumes a three-year B.Sc. program. If your university offers a four-year degree, use the additional year for an extended internship, advanced incident-response training, or a capstone security project.
Year 1
Foundation
Build IT and networking fundamentals

items.text: Learn computer architecture, operating systems, and file systems.
Study TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, ports, routing, and basic network troubleshooting.
Learn Linux command-line basics and Windows administration fundamentals.
Develop Python scripting skills and basic SQL knowledge.
Understand confidentiality, integrity, availability, authentication, and access control.
Practise reading system and authentication logs.

blocks.label: Project
blocks.text: Build a small lab that collects sample system logs and produces a basic report of login activity and unusual events.

blocks.label: Expected outcome
blocks.text: Explain how computers and networks work and interpret basic security-relevant logs.
Year 2
Security operations
Learn detection, monitoring, and investigation

items.text: Study common attack patterns, phishing, malware behavior, credential attacks, and privilege escalation concepts.

blocks.label: Learn SIEM fundamentals
blocks.text: event collection, searches, dashboards, alert rules, and correlation.

items.text: Explore endpoint security, firewall logs, authentication records, and basic cloud audit logs.
Practise incident severity classification, evidence documentation, and escalation.
Learn digital forensics fundamentals and evidence integrity.
Study the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and incident-response concepts.

blocks.label: Project
blocks.text: Build a defensive lab that ingests sample logs into a SIEM-style tool, detects suspicious authentication patterns, and generates investigation notes.

blocks.label: Industry exposure
blocks.text: Apply for SOC internships, security monitoring internships, or IT support roles that provide relevant security experience.
Year 3
Job readiness
Practise incident investigation and detection engineering

items.text: Learn alert correlation across endpoint, network, identity, and cloud logs.
Practise investigating phishing, suspicious logins, malware alerts, and unusual data access using safe datasets.
Write basic detection queries and improve rules to reduce false positives.
Learn incident timelines, case management, reporting, and shift handover procedures.
Understand threat intelligence, MITRE ATT&CK, and threat-hunting fundamentals.
Develop Python scripts for log parsing and basic enrichment.
Prepare for SOC interviews through timed, scenario-based investigations.

blocks.label: Capstone
blocks.text: Create an end-to-end SOC simulation with log ingestion, detection rules, alert triage, an incident timeline, and a final investigation report.

blocks.label: Expected outcome
blocks.text: Demonstrate structured, evidence-based alert investigation and clear incident documentation.

Windows, Linux, processes, permissions, event logs
Microsoft Sentinel, Splunk, Elastic Security or similar
Authentication, endpoint, firewall, DNS, cloud audit logs

Evidence integrity, timelines, file metadata, basic artifact analysis
Identity logs, audit trails, cloud configuration alerts
Incident tickets, severity rationale, handovers, investigation reports

blocks.text: You do not need to master every SIEM platform. Learn the common investigation workflow first, then become comfortable with one platform and its query language.
Build a portfolio using your own lab, authorized training platforms, or publicly available datasets. Keep all investigations defensive and within systems you are authorized to access.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Authentication log analyzer
Beginner
Use Python to parse sample authentication logs, summarize failed and successful logins, group events by source, and flag unusual patterns for review.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Python script, sample dataset, summary report, and documented detection limitations.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: Python, log parsing, Windows/Linux concepts, basic detection logic.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: SIEM detection and alert triage lab
Intermediate
In a local or authorized lab, ingest sample security events into a SIEM platform. Create detection rules for suspicious authentication behavior and investigate generated alerts.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Log sources, detection queries, test cases, alert severity rationale, and incident tickets.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: SIEM, log correlation, detection logic, investigation documentation.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Phishing investigation casebook
Intermediate
Analyze benign training samples or sanitized phishing artifacts. Examine sender information, URLs, message content, and available authentication evidence without opening unsafe attachments.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Investigation checklist, evidence summary, severity assessment, and recommended response actions.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: Email security, evidence handling, threat intelligence, incident reporting.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: End-to-end SOC incident simulation
Advanced

Investigate a simulated incident across authentication, endpoint, and network logs. Build a timeline, correlate evidence, map relevant behaviors to MITRE ATT&CK, and recommend proportionate containment and follow-up actions.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Detection rules, incident timeline, investigation report, and lessons-learned document.

blocks.label: Skills
blocks.text: Cross-source correlation, threat hunting, incident response, technical communication.

rows.text: Alert triage, SIEM monitoring, incident tickets
Identity monitoring, fraud-related alerts, access security
Cloud audit logs, endpoint and identity monitoring
Network traffic, firewall alerts, incident documentation
Vulnerability alerts, access reviews, incident support

blocks.text: Illustrative organizations to research include major IT service providers, cybersecurity consulting firms, managed security providers, and organizations with dedicated security operations teams. Examples include TCS, Infosys, Wipro, Accenture, IBM, and specialized security service providers. These are examples to investigate, not confirmation of current vacancies or eligibility.

blocks.label: Search terms
blocks.text: SOC Analyst Intern, SOC Analyst Tier 1, Security Operations Intern, Junior Cybersecurity Analyst, SIEM Analyst, and Incident Response Intern.

rows.text: Structure cybersecurity risk and response activities
Practise in controlled cybersecurity training environments

blocks.text: Possible certification pathways include entry-level cybersecurity credentials, vendor-specific SIEM training, and security operations courses. Check the current syllabus, exam requirements, price, and recognition before enrolling. Certifications are useful supplements, but practical investigations and clear reporting matter significantly.
Further study is optional for many entry-level SOC positions. It may help with research, security engineering, advanced forensics, or specialist roles.

rows.text: Malware analysis, threat hunting, and response workflows

blocks.text: Eligibility varies by institution. Some postgraduate technical programs require particular undergraduate subjects or entrance qualifications.

rows.text: Investigate cloud identity and resource alerts
Cloud logs, identity and access management
Assess threat information and adversary behavior

blocks.label: AI-assisted alert triage
blocks.text: Helping analysts summarize events and prioritize investigations, with human validation.

blocks.label: Extended Detection and Response (XDR)
blocks.text: Correlating security signals across endpoints, identities, networks, and cloud environments.

blocks.label: Cloud-native security monitoring
blocks.text: Investigating identity, API, workload, and configuration events.

blocks.label: Detection-as-code
blocks.text: Version-controlling and testing detection rules like software.

blocks.label: Automated incident workflows
blocks.text: Enriching alerts and carrying out approved repetitive response steps.

blocks.label: Identity threat detection
blocks.text: Identifying suspicious authentication patterns, privilege misuse, and compromised accounts.

blocks.label: Threat hunting analytics
blocks.text: Using behavioral baselines and cross-source evidence to find activity missed by individual alerts.
Automation can accelerate investigation, but analysts still need to verify evidence, understand context, and avoid treating a single alert or indicator as conclusive proof of compromise.
SOC Analyst readiness
Explain TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP/S, ports, and common network concepts
Read basic Windows and Linux security logs
Use a SIEM to search and correlate sample events
Explain common phishing, malware, and credential attack patterns
Write a Python script to parse or summarize logs
Classify alerts and document a clear severity rationale
Create an incident timeline and investigation report
Map relevant behaviors to MITRE ATT&CK where supported by evidence
Complete at least two defensive security lab projects
Explain escalation, evidence integrity, and safe incident-response practices
Reset checklist

By graduation, aim to present yourself as a cybersecurity graduate who can investigate security alerts, analyze logs, recognize suspicious behavior, document evidence, and follow incident-response procedures.
Prioritize five capabilities:

blocks.label: IT fundamentals
blocks.text: Networking, Windows, Linux, identity, and authentication.

blocks.label: Detection
blocks.text: SIEM searches, alert triage, and event correlation.

blocks.label: Investigation
blocks.text: Evidence-based analysis of phishing, suspicious logins, and endpoint alerts.

blocks.label: Automation
blocks.text: Python scripting and basic detection-rule development.

blocks.label: Portfolio
blocks.text: Defensive lab projects with investigation reports and reproducible results.
Your strongest entry-level positioning is: “I can monitor security events, investigate suspicious activity using logs and SIEM tools, and document clear, evidence-based incident findings.”
